comments.author: @LifewaysTravel
comments.text: Thanks for watching! Could you handle the freezing winters, powerful winds, and long distances from civilization? Or would the freedom and wide-open spaces make it worth it? Let me know in the comments! I'd love to hear your thoughts!

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: @lucyhallis9814 That makes perfect sense. ❤ Wyoming can feel incredible in summer, but the combination of harsh winters, strong winds, long distances, and limited access to medical care can be a very different story when you're thinking about living there full-time. I'd glad you still got to experience the beauty of Cody and the open spaces for yourself. Thanks for giving such an honest answer to the question!

replies.author: @lucyhallis9814
replies.text: I went to Wyoming in the summer.  I went to see the town of Cody back in 2006..  I'm a native Floridian and would have great difficulty with freezing winters (something I've never lived thru).  I don't like the wind and I've always lived in populated areas.  Being that I'm older and would have to live  within driving distance to a medical facility (thankfully I haven't had a medical emergency) but I wouldn't feel comfortable being hours away from a hospital or urgent care place.  Beautiful state though.

comments.author: @lucyhallis9814
comments.text: Live in Florida.  Have been to Wyoming on vacation.

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: What a great memory to share. ❤️ Going from the traffic around Orlando to those almost empty Wyoming highways at night must have felt like stepping into a completely different rhythm of life. Cody and the museums there clearly left an impression on you too. And running into someone from Wyoming again near Yellowstone years later is such a small-world moment. Thanks for coming back and sharing more of your experience with us!

replies.author: @lucyhallis9814
replies.text: @LifewaysTravel I went in 2006 and saw Cody Wyoming.  I was staying in Billings Montana. I enjoyed visiting the museums in Cody.  I live outside of Orlando, so traveling on an interstate or any highway in that area unless it's very late at night there is always traffic especially as you get closer to Disney. Disney traffic  is almost non-stop now unless it's very very early in the morning or in the wee hours of the morning.   That was very strange to me as I've driving down the highway in Wyoming and there is light traffic on a weekend night.  I remember years ago a woman that I knew who worked as cashier had lived in Wyoming back in the early 1980's (a rarity for someone living permanently in Florida) and had work in a gift shop near Yellowstone.  It was a much different lifestyle than living in Florida.

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: Sending a big hello to Florida! 🇺🇸❤️ Glad you’ve had the chance to experience Wyoming in person. Hope the documentary brought back some good memories from your trip. Thanks for watching with us!

comments.author: @schoolboy1325
comments.text: Nice video! My only major concern is the harsh winters. I will have to see how it really is.

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: That firsthand experience says a lot about how serious Wyoming winters can be. The wind, blowing snow, and road closures are no joke, especially in more remote areas. Owning land there sounds amazing, but you're right, growing your own food in that climate would definitely take some planning. Hope you get the chance to make that dream happen someday. 🌱❄️

replies.author: @schoolboy1325
replies.text: @LifewaysTravel I've only traveled through there during the winter. I didn't want to leave the vehicle due to the wind and blowing snow. Those roads used to always get shutdown. I've always wanted land out there. I used to always see it advertised. I also need to grow my own veggies, which is a challenge too.

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: That’s completely understandable. Wyoming winters can be intense, especially with the wind, snow, and sudden weather changes. Hopefully the video gave you a good starting point, but experiencing a winter there firsthand would definitely tell you the most. Thanks for watching! ❄️

comments.author: @WorldLivingTravel8
comments.text: Driving three hours across this state without seeing a single gas station or another human soul will humble anyone real quick
